utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Unfortunately Judge Thelin is unable to sit today. It is anticipated he shall be able to sit tomorrow. We have taken the view that it would be appropriate for us to continue the hearing pursuant to Rule 15 bis, and an order has been published and will be filed to that effect. The next witness, is it, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Mr. President, just for planning purposes, I believe in discussions with my colleagues across the well that we may well finish this witness today. And our next witness is not actually arriving until tomorrow evening or Saturday. So it may be that tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We get a long weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We get a long weekend. I don't think my colleagues opposite are complaining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you understand that the Chamber will be extremely reluctant.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I can see the look on your face, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As long as you understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can you hear me in the language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Russian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you read -- can you read that card that is being shown to you now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, would you be kind enough to take that affirmation, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The Russian channel for the witness is number 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, could you be sure that the witness is on number 8. Yes, Mr. Cayley.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Cayley:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you please give the Court your name.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Can I sit while --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Oh, of course. While you're giving evidence you can remain seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there a protection order here?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. This is public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You were asked for your name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oleg Safiulin, citizen of Russia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old are you, Mr. Safiulin?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts do you live?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I work in Moscow. My residence is in the town of Vologda.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are a reporter by profession. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, I am a reporter in the state television channel, mainly a reporter of documentary films. While I was in Yugoslavia, I was a reporter for the state news channel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in July of 1998 I believe you were the special correspondent for Russian state television. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, in 1998 I was a correspond, a special correspond, of the Russian state television for news bulletins. There is such a programme called "News."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And am I right in saying in July of 1998 Russian state television sent you to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, you're absolutely right. In 1998, in July, I was sent to Kosovo to work for the news programme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why were you sent to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: At that time it was the main news of international importance and all television channels had to have somebody in the so-called hotbeds of crisis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was happening in Kosovo that made events in the main news of international importance?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: There was a conflict on the scale of civil war between the Serbs and Albanians in that province, the Serbs and Albanians living in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, prior to your time in Kosovo, had you covered conflicts or civil wars in any other countries as a news correspondent?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes. I had experience of working in other crisis points. I had two missions two Chechnya as well as stints in Afghanistan and Dagistan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on this mission in 1998, where were any other staff members from RTR with you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I had with me a cameraman and a sound director. That is the usual composition of crews working in hot spots. On that occasion, our state company, the Russian television channel, decided to send three of us and I can name the other two members of the crew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the name of the cameraman?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Aleksandar Galanov, cameraman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the name of the sound engineer?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: The sound engineer was Viktor Mamaev.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'm right in saying that on the 15th of July, 1998, you flew from Moscow to Pristina in Kosovo. Is that right? Sorry, to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: On the 15th of July we arrived by plane from Moscow to Belgrade. And after having spent the night in Belgrade and renting a Volkswagen, in Belgrade, a car that I mentioned in my previous evidence, we set out for Pristina in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whereabouts did you stay in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: The name of the hotel was Grand. That is the central, main hotel where all the journalists, including foreign reporters stayed, from all parts of the world.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you speak Albanian?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to communicate, then, in Pristina if you didn't speak the language?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: At that time, Pristina was still a Serb town and we could communicate in Serb, in English. The Albanians who lived there know both Serbian and Albanian and even English. If they don't understand the question you put to them in English, you could ask it in Serb -- Serbian. And we had no problems eliciting information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have need of the Albanian language when you were working in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Of course the Albanian language was indispensable, and that is the reason why we hired an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the name of the interpreter you hired?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: His name was Shaban Hoti. He was a professor at the Pristina university, teaching the Russian language and literature. He was fluent in English, Russian, Albanian, and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown Prosecutor's Exhibit 54. And the ERN number of the particular photograph is U003-8696. Could you place it in front of the witness, to begin with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the individual in that photograph, sir?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise him. That is Shaban Hoti.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think that's fine, Mr. Usher. It's on Sanction so I think Their Honours can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many days after the 15th of July of 1998 did you spend in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: From the 16th July, all the time. I can't remember exactly the length of that stint. It could have been two weeks. Let me tell you exactly, until the 26th of July, maybe 25th. I can be mistaken by one day. If you need absolutely accurate information, I can find this out later, either by calling my work or checking documents. All the documents confirming our travel still exist and they are available.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want you to direct your mind to the 20th of July of 1998, and I'd like you to tell the Judges what you did on that day.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: On the eve of the 20th of July the previous crew introduced us to our interpreter, Shaban Hoti, and we agreed to set out on the 20th of July in the morning to go on a mission and make a news report from the Albanian side, because in the previous days we had already worked on the Serbian side. It's an international rule of journalism that when covering such conflicts it is necessary to cover both viewpoints in order to make an objective report. So we went to the Albanian side, knowing exactly in which place we can find --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I stop you there. I just want to clarify something because you stated that "on the eve of the 20th of July the previous crew introduced us to our interpreter and we agreed to set out on the 20th of July." Now, what day, what date, did you meet with the previous crew? If you set out on the 20th of July, what date was it that you met with the previous crew?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We didn't actually meet with the previous crew. We spoke on the phone and we missed each other on the way from Pristina to Belgrade. We had a telephone number of Shaban Hoti, and when we arrived in Pristina we called him immediately and he came to our hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what was the date that you set out on your mission? What was the date that you actually set out, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Monday, the 20th of July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: What did we need to know [as interpreted]? The direction, the name of the village -- what exactly do you need?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'd like to know is where you were actually heading off to in Kosovo from Pristina.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: From Pristina passing the Slatina airport driving towards Pec, we passed by one of the Serbian checkpoints and then we entered the territory that was currently held by Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to be absolutely clear, why, why were you heading in this direction? What had actually motivated you to go, as you say, "driving towards Pec" from Pristina through Slatina?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We had information to the effect that in that area we might find Albanians and that's why we headed there, because we needed to work on the Albanian side, too. At that time Albanians also had grievances against the Serb military. And I needed to make an unbiased report covering both sides of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any specific information you had about what the Albanians were doing in their particular area?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We had no specific information. We only knew that they held that area in the territory, which at that moment, as I said, was generally controlled by Serbs. In other words, we had information that we could find their so-called armed groups of combatants, and they were precisely who we wanted to meet.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown the next exhibit, and I think this is -- is this a new exhibit? This is part of P6. It's U007-2197.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Safiulin, do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: It is sufficiently difficult to say that this is precisely the place with absolute certainty, I can't do that. But I can say that 95 per cent it is the place. It is not a very fortunate photograph because you don't see the background in its entirety. If I could see all around this -- these vehicles and what is in the vehicle, I could confirm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: But it looks very much like it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is this place? What does it look very much like?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: That looks very much like the Serbian checkpoint, the last checkpoint you cross before you enter the territory held at that time by Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could please be shown from the same set of exhibits P6, and this is now U007-2199 -- oh, I'm sorry. This is a new exhibit. This is not part of P6. So if -- please, Mr. Registrar, we could have an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P87.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could look at that photograph. Do you recognise that view?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes. In this photo -- again, not with 100 per cent certainty, but you can see that this is the Serbian checkpoint and this section of the road leading to Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you place the photograph on the projector and just -- you mention the village Lapusnik. And if you could just point out to the Judges where you believe the village of Lapusnik to be.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Above the heads of the policemen in the background.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So just further purposes of the record on photograph U007-2199, Prosecutor's Exhibit 87, the witness is indicating the village of Lapusnik to be in the background of the photograph, immediately above the heads of the two police officers who are essentially in the middle of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would it be clarified whether he means the settlement that can be seen in the picture at about nose-and-mouth level of the person in the middle of the photograph, or does he mean a place further in the distance above the head?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, could you just indicate again with your pointer exactly where you believe the village of Lapusnik --

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think your description is better than mine. The houses to the left and right of the police officer in the middle at nose-and-mouth level, which again are in the background of the photograph. Is that clear enough now, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, what I'd like to show you now is Prosecutor's Exhibit 1, which is a map. And again I'm still interested -- yes -- in the location of the Serb checkpoint. If you can just --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: In fact, if you put the map in front of the witness so he can orientate himself on the map first, before we put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take a look, sir, at that map.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I took a look, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to show us where you believe the Serb checkpoint was located?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: The village Komorane is here just before Lapusnik, at the intersection. That's where the checkpoint was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you just point out Pristina to Their Honours so they -- if you can. Can you see Pristina?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Pristina -- that's the road from Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's the route you took? You travelled Pristina-Slatina- Komorane. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Right. From Pristina via Slatina airport and via Komorane. That Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was the last Serb checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What, if anything, did the policemen say to you at the checkpoint at Komorane?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: He said we shouldn't go on any further because it is dangerous. He said, We are not going to stop you. If you really want to go, go ahead, but it is a risk to your lives.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after you had received that warning, what did you do exactly?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We got into the car and went on and thanked the policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown 2199, which is the new photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know if you're going to be able to do this, but if you can indicate the route on this photograph that you took on from the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: There is a curve here, a zigzag here. We took that road straight on to Lapusnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So the witness is indicating on Prosecutor's Exhibit 87 that he essentially drove through the checkpoint and carried on -- straight on on the road you can see on the left-hand side of the photograph, disappearing up into the right-hand sort of background of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened to you as you drove along that road, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We travelled for maybe half a kilometre -- a kilometre and a half, 2 kilometres. I'm not sure exactly. Then we saw that the road was -- there was a barricade on the road. There was a barbed wire, a wire, and it was impossible to pass through in any passenger vehicle. We took the camera - I was driving - and we started shooting the footage. Then we approached the barricaded area. And then some people came out of the forest, armed people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you stop there. I would now like to show you Prosecutor's Exhibit 6, which is U007-2200. Do you recognise that photograph?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That's precisely what I had in mind, the anti-tank hedgehogs. And in front of them there were two cars turned upside down and some large boulders on the road so nobody could travel on that road. It was possible to continue on only riding on the right side of the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to be clear, what is this photograph? What does it represent?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: This is the area where the Albanian checkpoint was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said a moment ago that you saw barbed wire. Was there barbed wire on this checkpoint when you passed it?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: There were two cars turned upside down and there were two large -- there were large boulders brought here from elsewhere so that no cars could pass on. And then there was several pieces of barbed wire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these particular contraptions, I think you called them hedgehogs, did you see them at the checkpoint when you passed by them, sir, in July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you answer again because I didn't get a translation. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. In July, on the 20th of July, 1998, these anti-tank hedgehogs were located near the village of Lapusnik at the Albanian checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you began filming and some people came out of the forest, armed people. How many people came out of the forest?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Initially about five to seven people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Some of them wore civilian clothes and had automatic weapons and some of them wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these people speak to you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Well, we spoke to them because we had to speak to them before they started shooting at us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, who was in the vehicle at this time? Who was with you accompanying you when you were at the Albanian checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I was driving. Shaban Hoti, our interpreter, sat to my right; and in the back, Sasha Galanov, our cameraman; and sound technician Mamaev.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the nature of the conversation that you had with these armed individuals at the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We asked them for permission to pass through, to travel into their territory. And we told them that we wanted to hear what was their life like, what complaints they had. We wanted to hear more about the situation that existed in Kosovo at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did they say to you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, we also said to them that we were aware that they had evidence of the fact that Serbs were shooting civilians and we asked them to show us where those events had happened. They told us, No, you can't see any of that. You should turn back.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness can be shown map 6 again from P1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the location of the Albanian checkpoint that you're now speaking of, do you have an approximate idea of where that checkpoint was located?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Right in front of the village itself. We could even say that in the centre, right after the turn. This spot here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which village are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Lapusnik village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you put a mark on the map indicating where you believe that the checkpoint was located with a pen.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: So just for clarity, and I suspect we'll have to give this a new exhibit number, the witness has marked a cross where he believes that the checkpoint -- the Albanian checkpoint was located.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P88.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the individuals that you met at the checkpoint, you said they were armed, some in uniform, some in civilian clothing. Did you come to any conclusion as to which army they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: They were not members of any army. They were simply members of the resurgency [as interpreted]. I can say that because I had previous experience from contacts with members in other countries. This was a well-armed unit, well-disciplined, with a clear chain of command. A very firm one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that they were "well-disciplined, with a clear chain of command." Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: First of all, I could see how they communicated with each other. At the checkpoint, there was one person who was of higher rank and then there was several subordinates of his, and there were what are normally called ordinary soldiers, rank-and-file soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How could you tell that there was a person of higher rank at the checkpoint? How could you identify him?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: It wasn't difficult because when he spoke everybody else shut up. Everybody listened to his orders and he was the one deciding whether we should continue or turn back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that you in fact turned back. How far did you drive in the opposite direction?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We travelled for some 900 metres, perhaps, and then stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And if the witness could be shown 2200 again which is part of P6, just so that we're clear about the direction in which you travelled. And if it could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that you travelled 900 metres. Can you just indicate in which direction you travelled on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We travelled in the opposite direction. We went behind this curve, this turn here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the witness is indicating on the photograph that he travelled back away from the hedgehogs in the middle of the road, sort of upwards into the background of the photograph and away to I think some houses that you can see in the background. I'm right in saying that you were essentially travelling back towards Pristina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. We travelled back towards Pristina, back towards the Serbian checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've said that you travelled for about 900 metres. When you travelled 900 metres, can you tell the Judges what happened after you stopped.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We saw a large passenger bus without any windows. It was bullet-riddled. And in the back of it, there was a destroyed house. What probably happened is that as a bus travelled on the road somebody opened fire from the house and then the bus was hit. It wasn't clear who did the shooting, whether it was people on the Serbian side or on the Albanian side, so we decided to stop and investigate. We could see not -- no bodies around there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you get out of the car?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, we got out of the car, put our camera on a tripod and started shooting the footage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened after you started shooting the footage?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We practically completed shooting the footage, packed the camera, and went back to the car. And at the same time we saw that there were armed -- well-armed people running towards us. One had an anti-tank grenade launcher and there were several sniper rifles and so on, so they stopped us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these well-armed people running towards you, can you describe to the Judges how they were dressed.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Just like the people at the checkpoint. Some of them were the people that I had seen at the checkpoint. And then there was some other well-armed people accompanying them wearing camouflage uniforms. So we could conclude that the entire road was under their control. They were on both sides of the road because they appeared very fast after we stopped our car at that stop. It is not easy to run the distance of 900 metres, especially when carrying weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were these individuals members of the Serb security forces or someone else?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: No. They were not Serbs. They were Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when these people came running towards you, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We tried to drive away because we knew what fate expected us, however our car was not a very powerful one and we would not have been able to escape the fire had we tried to drive away in a Volkswagen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what did you do?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We stopped and waited until they reached us and followed their orders. They told us to turn around and go back to the checkpoint from where we had originally travelled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you in fact do that? You went back to the checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes. One of them got into our car. He had weapons on him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If -- just for absolute clarity, because we're speaking about two checkpoints, if the witness could be shown Prosecutor's 6, U007-2700.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say you travelled back to the checkpoint, is that the checkpoint which you travelled back to?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes. So for the second time on that day we went back to that checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you got to that checkpoint -- well, actually one question before that. By the time you got to this checkpoint, can you just confirm again who was with you at this time, who was in the car with you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Shaban Hoti, the interpreter; Sasha Galanov, the cameraman; Viktor Mamaev, the sound engineer; and myself. I was driving. And with us was the armed man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you got back to the -- what you've called the Albanian checkpoint, what happened there?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: They stopped our car, not in front of the hedgehogs, the anti-tank hedgehogs, but we rather drove around them on the right side of the road. We travelled around the checkpoint and got behind the barricades. So finally we found ourselves on the Albanian territory, which is precisely where we wanted to go initially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you had got to the other side of the barricade, what happened next?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We were taken out of the car. Our camera, money, and other belongings were confiscated. Our car was driven to the other side. We were taken to the forest and made to face the forest, and they started cocking the weapons behind us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you can recall and looking at the photograph, which side of the road were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Towards the forest, closer to the forest. If you see this elevated area here, this is the area where the forest -- so they took us in that direction. As I'm facing the photograph now, this is on the right side. If you see this elevation, this small hill, the forest begins on it. So they took us in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Just to be clear, the witness is indicating on Prosecutor's Exhibit 2200 [sic] that he was taken to the right-hand side of the photograph, where there can be seen a slight elevation coming up from the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that weapons were cocked. What did you believe was going to happen at this point?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't difficult to conclude what was going to happen. We assumed that they were going to kill us. Because if we apply the military war rules, we could see that we disobeyed their orders and we were now in their hands and they could do with us what they pleased.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you previously referred to the organisation and discipline of the group that you had originally met at the Albanian checkpoint. The group that you were now with of these Albanian soldiers, how did you find their organisation and discipline?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Well, as I realised later, it was a unit and it was located in several spots at the barricade, at the checkpoint, in the forest, and further down the road. The person in charge was the one who did not let us pass through. However, there were a lot of people coming and going. And the one who took us to the forest started issuing orders and his orders were carried out very fast.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you spend in the forest?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: An hour and a half to two hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that period of time had passed, the hour and a half to two hours, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: During hour and a half to two hours, there were a lot of communication going on, radio communication; new commanders were arriving in vehicles; they were their superiors replacing them. And finally, as we understood, the top commander arrived. He wore a very clean uniform with polished shoes, NATO camouflage uniform, and he had a pistol on him. He was the one who decided our fate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions to clarify. You say that communications were going on, radio communications. Who was engaging in radio communications?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: One of the mid-level commanders constantly passed information to some of his deputies, as we understood it. So they constantly communicated among each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say it was a form of radio communications, what sort of equipment did you see?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: It was ridiculous-looking equipment. They looked like toys and looked like something you could buy in any shop. We could conclude that their walkie-talkies did not have very large range. So based on that we again concluded that the people they communicated with were not very far away, perhaps just 500 metres away. They had more powerful walkie-talkies but they didn't use them as often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that new commanders were arriving in vehicles. How did you know they were commanders? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain that. But when a general walks into the barracks everyone stands upright and stands at attention, the same thing was going on there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you're saying when the people you thought were commanders were arriving other individuals that were there reacted to them coming. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes. They were disciplined and they listened to what was said by the newly arrived commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this last commander that you describe with polished shoes and NATO uniform, I'd like to show you a photograph which is I think P --

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This is U008-1567, and it will need an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P89.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Safiulin, do you recognise this individual?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: A long time has passed since 1998, so it is difficult to say with a hundred per cent certainty that this is the same commander. But I'm about 98 per cent sure that this is the same person. He looked younger, but six years have passed since. However, I can't claim with hundred per cent certainty that this is him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, which commander is this?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: The man to whom everybody was subordinated at the time when we were detained.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did this man arrive at the checkpoint, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Two hours later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just one question I have for you. You were in the forest at this time. How far from the road were you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: About 100 metres. However, it was not a forest. It was edge of the forest. You know, this is where the forest started and we were about 60 metres from the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you have a clear view of the road from where you were in the forest?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes. We had a clear view, but only of the trees in front of us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So how could you see what was going on on the road? How could you see these commanders arriving?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: He came up to us and talked to us. Every time somebody new arrived, they would come up and talk to us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after this gentleman arrived, what happened to you after that?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Several other cars arrived. We were split into groups and taken inside the territory under the Albanian control. We did not have any documents on us, no money, no camera, just the clothes we had on us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say "we were split into groups." Who was split into groups?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: The interpreter was taken away immediately within those two hours, a bit more than two hours. As I saw later, the car travelling with the interpreter travelled for some 800 metres and stopped at the base of a hill. The three of us were taken to Lapusnik. We passed the houses, and then the car stopped. We were taken out of the car in a vacant area, a field perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, am I right in saying that you and the other two members of the TV crew were in one car together?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your interpreter, Shaban Hoti, had been taken immediately, you say. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: No. All of us together left the checkpoint, as I told you. But after we moved away, the three of us, the three Russians were placed in one car and Shaban was placed in another car. Our car stopped at the bottom of this hill and Shaban's car travelled another 800 metres up the elevation. And then I saw their car stop as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I could just show you the map which is P1. And if you recall at all in which direction you travelled from the checkpoint. If you can't, say so. This is -- I think it's map 6. So what I'm interested in now is the journey from the checkpoint to this next point that you reached where Mr. Shaban Hoti was 800 metres in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just say it is not a big issue but it is a matter of principle: I think when maps are being put to witnesses to identify various directions in which they are said to have travelled, it is not useful for those maps to be marked in any way. And of course this exhibit has a nice big red square box around it. So it may not be the most useful way of proceeding. Your Honour, that's my only suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Is the suggestion, Your Honour, that we take all the markings of the towns off the map? Because that seems ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, Mr. Cayley. No, Mr. Cayley. The issue really is whether this map should be marked or a separate one for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: We're talking just now -- which marking are we speaking of?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The one you are asking the witness to make.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Oh, of course, yes. I was just showing -- I'm going to show him the other map on which he placed the cross and I'm going to ask him to mark that map. And if in fact he can be shown this one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The same map that was used by the witness before would be the one, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I think this map solves the problem my learned friend has opposite, because it doesn't have a box.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If he's marked one I think the witness should mark the same one.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I agree. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could mark approximately, if you know, the location which you arrived at after you left the Albanian checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if you could mark that cross with a "2."

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And the witness has marked "1" where he believes the Albanian checkpoint to be and "2" the spot where he believes he travelled back to after he left the checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can you tell the Judges what happened when you got to the point that you've marked 2.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We were taken out of the car and we were led down the slope towards the edge of the forest. There were three trenches surrounded by big rocks. They told us not to stop. They -- to look away from the road. And we heard again the cocking of rifles. They were inspecting the car, the boot, the hood, the inside of the car. We heard the sounds of them inspecting the car. They turned on and off the headlights. They checked everything, and it was clear that if they found anything suspicious we didn't have long left to live.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "we were taken out of the car," who was taken out of the car at this point?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: The sound engineer, Mamaev; the cameraman, Galanov; and myself. We were left to stand in front of those three heaps of rocks ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did you feel at this time?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Well, we understood clearly that it's finished with jokes. And if those people found anything suspicious, because it was clear they had already began -- begun to think of us as spies, they would simply spill gas on us and light up a match. That's what we thought was ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were your colleagues dealing with the situation at the time as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Sasha was very worried. Mamaev, who is a very young man and experiencing such a situation for the first time, was certainly worried inside, maybe showing it less. It's very difficult to describe anybody's personal reaction in a situation when they clearly realise that their life could be about to end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you're referring to Sasha you're referring to Sasha Galanov?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes. Aleksandar Galanov.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you wait by the side of the road next to these objects I think you've described as sort of stones or rocks?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: 40 minutes perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after this 40 minutes, after the search of the vehicle, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: After that we were split again. First they took away Galanov. They put me behind the wheel of the car in which we arrived. Mamaev was put in the car together with me. He was made to sit face-down between seats so that he wouldn't be seen from outside. And two armed men sat in the car with us. And they made us drive towards the nearby 2 house. When we arrived there, they made me get out of the car, twisted my arms behind my back and took me inside the house. It was obviously not a residential house because there was no --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that Galanov was taken away. Where was Galanov taken?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: They took him to that same house, only ahead of us, whereas Mamaev and I were brought there later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were you able to find your way to this house?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: The guard who was sitting next to me in the passenger's seat was showing me where to go; left, right, straight on, left, right.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If you could be shown again the map that you've marked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this particular house that you were taken to, this building that you were taken to, do you have any idea where it is located?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I think it lies very close down the road from the first marking I made -- from the second marking I made. Because I remember very clearly when it all ended well for us, I returned to that place again and I can say pretty safely that after you pass Lapusnik you can control the upper road and the lower road sitting in that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: And the witness has marked another cross "3" the location of the building where he was taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just one point, Witness, to clarify. As one is travelling from Pristina to Pec, on which side of the road is this building located? So travelling from Pristina to Pec, which side of the road is this building located?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: The left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you said earlier on that the soldier gave you directions, left, right, straight on, to get there. Did you go directly down the main road to this building or did you go on a more circuitous route?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We circled around for a while using byroads before we came to that house. We didn't take the shortcut.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say that when you got to this building your arm was twisted behind your back --

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: When they were getting us -- hauling us, I would say, out of the car.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: They hauled us into that house where I saw Galanov; he was already sitting there, face to the wall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you and Mamaev were taken into the building. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what happened when you got into the building?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: They blindfolded us straightaway, brought a plank, laid it -- threw it on the cement floor, and they told us, Sit here and wait.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you wait there for?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: It could have been two, three hours. We were not allowed to talk. They told us to sit there and be quiet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there anybody else with you? Was it the three of you alone or was somebody else there with you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: A guard was with us at all times, an armed guard. Maybe you will ask me how could you see that he was armed? I could see the -- I could hear the sound of cocking of the rifle. I could hear the sound of his -- putting the rifle on his shoulder or across his breast -- across his chest. And these guards changed constantly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say you waited for two or three hours. After that period of time, what happened?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: After that, there arrived one of the most superior commanders, I would say, with his bodyguards. They told me to take off the blindfold and answer their questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: If the witness could be shown I think the last photograph, which is I think a new exhibit, U008-1566. And if I could have an exhibit number for that, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Prosecution Exhibit P90.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this photograph, P90?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: To say with absolute certainty that this is the man we just discussed is something that I cannot do. But at least I can say that it is not that main commander who interrogated us; of that I am certain. With this man it's possible we talked before meeting the chief commander. From the moment I took off the blindfold I was allowed not to put it on again. And this man told me that Shaban, our interpreter, had been arrested and he would not be travelling with us any more. But this is not "the chief," as they called him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's possible you saw this man in the building?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes. That is very possible. He was wearing civilian clothes and he had on his sleeve a sort of armband that is normally worn by blue helmets and the people who work with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did this man say to you about Shaban Hoti? He said that Shaban wouldn't be travelling with you any more. Did he say anything else to you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: He said that Shaban was misrepresenting himself, holding himself out to be someone he was not, and that was the main source of our problems and that was why we were being held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything further about Shaban Hoti to you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: He said that Shaban had been arrested. He didn't actually say it. He made a gesture meaning arrested, crossing his lower arms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after your blindfold had been taken off and the main commander arrived, you say that he interrogated you. What questions did he ask you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: It all began with his question when we arrived in Belgrade, when we arrived in Pristina, how we turned up where we were, what we were looking for in Pristina. Then he started asking where I was born, what school I completed, which university I went to, who my teachers were, what was the subject of my diploma paper, what I majored in, how many children I had, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how long were you interrogated?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: With every person, 40 minutes. After me, it was Galanov's turn and then Mamaev's.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned Shaban Hoti being arrested. Did you see Shaban Hoti again during this time?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: When I took off my blindfold, I did see Shaban Hoti because he was the one interpreting the interrogation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you describe how Shaban Hoti looked at this time?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: It was clear that he had been beaten. He had a haematoma on his face, blood on his trousers, on his shirt and on his shoes as well, and he was very frightened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that he was very frightened?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: He was simply shaking with fear. There was a lost look in his eyes -- what do you mean how I could see? It's obvious when somebody's frightened.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've explained it very well. Now, after the interrogation had been completed, can you recall Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. if anything else was said to you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: They didn't say anything clearly. They said, Sit here and wait, and then set out to take Shaban away. I said, What are you going to do with Shaban? They said, He's going to wage war on our side to prove the kind of patriot he is. Then later when he was gone they added Shaban was not the person he was holding himself out to be; he was really working for the Serbian police. And since you came with him, you, too, must be Serbian spies. And under the laws of war, you have to be punished and executed, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after this had been stated to you, what happened after that?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: After that, everybody was gone and it became very quiet. Somebody drove away in our car as well and we were left there alone with a guard. And it continued all the way until dusk.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For how many hours after the interrogation did you remain in the building?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Maybe another two or three hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at dusk what happened?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: After that the commander came back, brought mineral water, half a loaf of bread, some sort of cheese bread. He said, Here, you can have a drink. It looks like nothing bad is going to happen to you now. You can sit here and wait some more. And that's the last thing he said. We didn't see him anymore until dark. When it was already dark we were all put into a car, the same car we actually arrived in, and started driving us -- again not taking a direct road, but around and around, obviously trying to confuse us, and took us out of the car again after they stopped, without taking off our blindfolds. At the place we stopped there were three haystacks. I remember it as if it were yesterday. As they were standing there they were again talking on their radios. And that was our last trial and tribulation before we were driven to the checkpoint again. But at that point, we were still thinking they were going to kill us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say you had a blindfold -- they took off your blindfold. Where were you blindfolded?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: They blindfolded us when they took us into that house, immediately. They took it off during the interrogation and put it on back again after the interrogations. And afterwards, I was the only one who was allowed to take off the blindfold.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were you blindfolded with, if you can remember?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I remember it was a child's T-shirt, black, torn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say you were the only one that had your blindfold taken off. Whereabouts were you when the blindfold was taken off?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: To determine the location where we were when my blindfold was taken off, I was unable. It was already dark. After that the main chief commander who interrogated us showed up again and told me, You were the one who was the driver. Here is your equipment, your documents, your stuff. You will sit behind the wheel now, turn left, and we'll see if you're going to reach the Serbian side because it's already dark and Serbs shoot at any moving object when it's dark. He told me, Drive away, turn left, and don't come back again. That was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What language were you speaking at this time?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: English and Serbian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the commander was able to communicate with you in English and Serbian?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned the three haystacks where you were taken. I just want to be clear. What happened at the three haystacks?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: They spoke on their radios for a long time, 30, 40 minutes. They were making jokes, laughing. It was obvious they were either in a good mood or tipsy, had a drink. In any case, we thought that people in that mood would find it easy to shoot us. They didn't obviously care what was going to happen to us. However, somebody somewhere must have taken the decision to release us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the commander who gave you back your equipment, did that happen at the three haystacks?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, practically next to them. And he took us back to the car. He told me to check if everything was right and drive away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you say you turned -- that they told you to turn left on to the road. Which road did you turn left on to?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: It was the Pristina-Pec road before the barricades. Before that when I was taking a turn the barricades were on the right -- sorry, on the left, 300 metres before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you turned left, in which direction were you going when you turned left onto the main road?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: When I turned left, I went straight on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And whereabouts were you going towards? Were you going towards Pristina or Pec?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We headed for Pristina towards the Serbian checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned the barricade. Did you in fact see the barricade again when you were going towards Pristina?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, I saw it. From the bend, they were 300 metres away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And here we're talking about which? We're talking about the Serbian checkpoint or the Albanian checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the Albanian checkpoint. I was going uphill. There was the Albanian checkpoint on the right and the Serbian checkpoint was about -- was on the left, further away, closer to Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did it take you to get to the Serbian checkpoint?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Seven, ten minutes, not more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you got back to Pristina, did you report this matter to the local authorities?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes. We went to the police station, told the whole story.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you report this matter anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: The next day I called Shaban's daughter to tell her that Shaban was taken captive and I called my office to tell them what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honour, for this witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cayley. That sounds as though we've reached a convenient time for the break. We will resume at 5 past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Mr. Topolski has agreed to go first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's always nice to find a volunteer, isn't it? Cross-examined by Mr. Topolski:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Safiulin, I represent a defendant in these proceedings called Isak Musliu and I have some questions for you. I hope not to keep you too long. Could I ask you first of all please: Did RTR Television have a particular position regarding the KLA in 1998?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We work in the information service, and for us there are no positions with regards to which side is right, which side shall be considered as wrong or guilty. Our job for reporters of information and news channels, the main goal is reflect both sides. When we go on a business trip, we are not being instructed to fulfill any task or omission, we should only act as reporters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your television station therefore had no editorial position as far as this conflict was concerned; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I have said what I said. No specific tasks were raised before us with regards to whether we should shoot coverage only on one side and not on the other or any other missions of this nature. We had only to shoot our coverage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have been yourself in other crisis points as you described them, war zones perhaps as I shall describe them, is that right, before 1998?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you ever found yourself in the situation where you had been detained before by one side or another?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: In this specific case, like in this specific case I don't think I had any circumstances before. We used to work on different sides of the barricade, if I may say so, in different conflicts and wars. And we managed to work on both sides, on the sides of both parties to such conflicts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That wasn't quite, sir, what I asked you. The question actually was: Had you ever been detained before by a side in a conflict that you were reporting on?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: There were some incidents when I was detained in Chechnya.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have before us, the lawyers and the Court, two documents relating to your evidence. The first is described as a statement and was taken from you at the Moscow City Northern Administrative District Prosecutor's Office on the 23rd of December of 2003. Do you recall being at the prosecutor's office and making a statement? A copy of which is I think available, just for you to have a look at.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm grateful to Mr. Younis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall being there and making this statement?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, I remember. We were summoned to the prosecutor's office on the 23rd of December and our statement was taken there, as you just observed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In addition to that and later than that, indeed on the 16th of September of 2004, again in the city of Moscow, do you recollect, Mr. Safiulin, being asked a number of questions by Mr. Lehtinen, an investigator of the ICTY? Again --

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lehtinen was present at the second interrogation and he put questions to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, Mr. Younis, has provided very kindly a copy for you to look at. I don't ask you anything about it at the moment; I just want to confirm the fact of it. Can I now turn to the 20th of July, 1998 itself. When you left Pristina with your colleagues and with interpreter Shaban Hoti, what was your destination?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We wanted to proceed to the Albanian side and to work on their side because we had already completed our coverage on the Serbian side. We had already done the portion of our reporting on the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I used the word "destination" in my last question I was trying to be specific. Were you aiming for a particular place?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We had the information regarding the places where Albanians could be found and which territories they held under their control. And those were several places -- we had several places in mind, and Lapusnik was not the only place we had in mind. Before we used to be in other places, in other territories held by Albanians and we used to work there freely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you headed for the village of Lapusnik itself or some other place?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: At that period of time, I did not know that that village was called Lapusnik, but I had an idea where Albanian combatants could be found, in which areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reason I ask you the question in that way is because in the first of the statements that you made on the 23rd of December of 2003, these words appear: "At about 8.00 in the morning of the 20th of July, we left with our interpreter for the village of Lapusnik to shoot some footage and get some information from the Albanians." Do you recollect saying that in this statement?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely right, I said. But about 8.00 on the 20th of July, I was not aware of this. The interrogation was taking place on the 23rd of December, 2003. By then I already knew in which direction I was going or where I was going, that is why I named that village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to take your journey that day in stages. Could you please have put before you the photographs you were looking at earlier on, that is to say the photograph of a roadblock or barricade at P87 and the photograph P6. Did you or anyone in your car take these photographs?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: No, we did not take these pictures. We did not have any equipment to take such pictures. We had only video equipment with us, namely a video camera, and we had no regular cameras with us.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the photograph of the men, one of whom is leaning on a car --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Part of P87.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you look at that photograph and look at the houses in the distance, that, I agree, is the area in which the village of Lapusnik is located, and you've already mentioned that. To the right of the photograph as we look at it, in other words beyond the Jeep and the pile of tires, I want to ask you this: Were you aware of deployment of Serb forces in that area?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: No, we were not aware. Moreover, the picture which -- the pictures which are shown here were taken much later, after the 20th of July because on the 20th of July the checkpoint had a different appearance. There was no combat vehicle on the checkpoint. There were only regular cars and some people with machine-guns, maybe a few heavy machine-guns. And we were not aware of any other troops there at this location.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For example, when you were stopped first by the Serbs at the Serb checkpoint, did anyone there tell you, You better be careful, we have soldiers off the road in the direction of Lapusnik, snipers. Did anyone mention that to you?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: We were told that, You better be careful, in general. We do not advise you to go to the Albanian side. But with regard to snipers or any other troops which might be there, we were not warned of them. Had we seen a sniper, this would have been a bad sniper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not sure what I understand by a good sniper. But I shall move on. I want you to look at the photograph of the items lying in the road. I'll hold up mine so you can see the one I'm talking about. It's part of P6 -- it is P6 I think. Mr. Safiulin, if you look over to me, it's this photograph. You have it there. Thank you. As of the 20th of July, that is to say the day you were on this road as to opposed to the day on which this photograph may have been taken, would you agree with me that there was a barricade made of in part rocks, stones and one or two old vehicles, perhaps, just around this bend that we see on this photograph here? Is that your recollection of how it was on the day?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Well, at this picture we can see only the so-called anti-tank hedgehogs, and right behind them there were two tipped-over cars and some boulders and pieces of rock.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you now about the place where you were taken for your interrogation. You've described it in your statement in December 2003 in this way: a building made of concrete, concrete floor and concrete walls. I take those words from your statement of December 2003. From September 2004, the question-and-answer session with Mr. Lehtinen, you described it as "a single-storey permanent post... not exactly a residential home."

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I said that it was -- that building could have been used as a one-storey post. But I did not say that it was a post. This building could have been used as a post because it was very well-situated. And in that building nobody resided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This location, Mr. Safiulin, could in due course in this case be important and I want to be clear what you're saying about it. Is it the case that you could see the Peja-Pristina road from this building? That's my first question.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, I can say so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My second question is: Could you see this building from the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Peja-Pristina road?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, we could see that building from the road Pec-Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you about the circumstances that led to your being detained. In evidence in chief, in other words when Mr. Cayley was asking you questions, you used the expression "we disobeyed their orders." What I want to suggest to you, Mr. Safiulin, is that your behaviour and that of your crew that day could -- could -- have been considered provocative. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: No, I do not agree. At that point the Albanians were not controlling the law and the territory of Kosovo. I had the accreditation issued by the foreign ministry, the so-called workers' [phoen] card and I can tender it in evidence. I had the right to work in the territory and disobey the people who in whatever manner controlled that territory or gripped control of that territory. I did not need any permissions from the Albanian side to conduct the coverage in the Autonomous Region of Kosovo; I already had accreditation from the official authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I wasn't intending to indicate you would succeed in an action in a court of law about this, but the way you behaved on the street, as it were. And let me be clear what I mean. You were stopped by KLA soldiers. Right?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, we were stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were told to turn around and go back. Correct?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes, we were told so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within 3 kilometres you'd stopped and started filming with a video camera.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: In 800 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 800 metres. You were filming with a video camera?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You had previously been stopped by Serbs and warned about going on at all down that road. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: Yes. This was already mentioned in the documents presented to you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Leaving one side completely what Serbs may or may not have told you, looking at what we've just agreed you did from the KLA's point of view, sir, I repeat: What you did could by them have been considered somewhat provocative. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I cannot know what could be their interpretation of those actions. I can say again that I had the official accreditation from the state authorities and I had the right to work in those areas in which -- where I was allowed to work at that stage of the conflict. And did not need even to ask the permission from the Albanian combatants where I am allowed to work and not allowed to work, especially bearing in mind that I was not in the territory under their control but I was already a distance from their post. And the rule of a journalist, as everybody knows, if you're being pushed out through the door, go in through the window. I needed to make a good coverage and I made a good coverage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sure you're as courageous a journalist as Russia could provide. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: I'm believe that you're a most assertive lawyer who can convince the high court and the accusation in your points [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened to your film, the film you took that day?

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
utterances.text: The film was kept by the Albanians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about something that you talked about when you were interviewed in September 2004. Do you remember being asked a question regarding what Shaban Hoti looked like and what you knew about him? You then gave a description of him to Mr. Lehtinen. And I just want to read you, Mr. Safiulin, if I may just one line from this answer of yours to the ICTY investigator. "We later asked one of Shaban Hoti's friends if Shaban collaborated with the Serbian police, and he told us that he did. However, Shaban Hoti himself had never given us to understand that he could be linked to the Serbian police in any way."

utterances.speaker: OLEG IUNUSOVICH SAFIULIN
